fact: Eswatini's Ministry of Education and Training, with UNICEF and HISP Uganda, integrated disability indicators into its DHIS2-based national EMIS and trained over 900 school administrators and focal teachers on the updated data-capture tools.
The Ministry of Education and Training, with UNICEF Eswatini support, proposed DHIS2 for Education through an initial pilot project in 2020, replacing its paper and MS Access based collection.

GPE KIX reports that in the 2025 reporting cycle the Annual Education Census recorded submissions from 129 primary and 14 secondary schools and the 16th Day Survey from 17 schools, collected through the Ministry of Education and Training's national EMIS.
DHIS2 for Education says Eswatini's Ministry of Education and Training is modernising its EMIS with DHIS2, a transition begun in 2020 that replaced a centralised MS-Access system.

DHIS2 for Education describes a fully operational Eswatini EMIS that served as the source for the country's 2022 UIS reporting on enrolments, repeaters and staffing and produced a 2026 bursary list for orphans and vulnerable children.
DHIS2 for Education says the Eswatini DHIS2 implementation supports school-level and learner-level data and introduces unique personal identification numbers (PINs).
GPE KIX says Eswatini's fully digital, PIN-driven EMIS, nationally launched in March 2024, covers all 976 primary and secondary schools and provides aggregate enrolment numbers.
GPE KIX says Eswatini's PIN-driven EMIS introduced individual-level student and staff tracking across all 976 schools.
